submission.rationale: At decision time (52 h) the receiving fermentation shows an abrupt DO2 collapse from ~10.2 mg/L to ~4.3 mg/L between 50.0 and 52.0 h — a distinctive oxygen-demand excursion not present in any source batch, which maintained 9–11 mg/L at that process age. DO is still above the 2.0 mg/L minimum but trending downward into the remaining ~44 h of high-productivity operation. The source-calibrated forward model indicates that keeping current operation, increasing air alone, or even a combined moderate intervention would all violate the 2.0 mg/L oxygen limit (min DO 1.36, 1.53, 1.65 mg/L respectively), while only a strong feed reduction keeps DO at 2.58 mg/L with zero below-limit hours. Strong feed reduction also retains the highest counted product mass (256 kg nominal vs 201–230 kg for weaker interventions) because it preserves oxygen availability and continued productive operation, whereas a stop would yield zero counted production. Given the imminent and modeled oxygen constraint violation, the bounded intervention with the strongest oxygen relief and no production loss is recommended.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect: it uses an estimated transfer multiplier (0.52) and assumed parameters rather than the hidden receiving realization. Even strong_feed_reduction has one of five sensitivity members dipping to 1.31 mg/L, so feasibility is not guaranteed; hidden receiving kinetics could differ further. DO observations show a step change suggesting possibly a sensor artifact or a real sudden demand event, which the model cannot distinguish. Product mass range under this action spans 201–623 kg, reflecting substantial model uncertainty. Delayed assays (P) lag by 4 h, so current true product state is partially unobserved. If DO continues falling despite the intervention, escalation or stop may be needed.

submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~10.2 to ~4.3 mg/L between t=50 and t=52 h and continues to decline — an oxygen-demand spike unseen in any source batch. While 4.3 mg/L is still above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, the sustained downward trend threatens a constraint violation, and product (P=2.88 g/L at 48h) is actively accumulating, so stopping or cutting feed would sacrifice product mass. Increasing aeration (×1.15) directly counteracts the elevated oxygen uptake with no production penalty and restores DO margin; feed reduction is held in reserve if DO2 fails to recover. No extra assay is requested because the online DO2 sensor already establishes the abnormality and a 4h assay delay would postpone mitigation.
submission.uncertainty: The hidden cause of the DO drop (e.g., substrate pulse vs sensor fault) is unknown; if it is transient, increase_air is harmless but unnecessary, and if demand grows faster than 15% more aeration can supply, a further step (combined or strong_feed_reduction) may be needed. DO2 trajectory after intervention cannot be predicted exactly; the ~-0.2 mg/L/h decline rate extrapolated from 50.2-52.0 h could reach ~2 mg/L in roughly 10 h if unaddressed, though this extrapolation is uncertain (only ~2 h of post-drop data).

Receiving P assay at t=48h = 2.57 g/L vs source-1 3.06, source-2 3.02, source-3 2.98 g/L at the same age
DO2 at decision time (52.0h) = 1.13 mg/L, lowest reading in the record
Source batches under KEEP never dropped below ~7.4 mg/L, confirming the receiving vessel has a distinct, worse oxygen balance
Allowed action bounds: strong_feed_reduction = feed 0.6, air 1.15; combined = feed 0.8, air 1.15; keep = 1.0/1.0
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation is in a sustained, worsening oxygen-constraint violation: DO2 fell abruptly at 46.2h from ~10 mg/L to ~1.1-1.7 mg/L and remains ~1.13 mg/L at the 52h decision time, well below the 2.0 mg/L minimum. The 15% aeration increase alone (increase_air) is unlikely to close a gap of this magnitude given the ~9 mg/L deficit relative to pre-crash levels, and KEEP guarantees continued violation. A feed reduction lowers oxygen uptake demand directly and, unlike stop, retains the accumulated product mass and keeps production counting. I select the bounded strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) because it combines the largest demand reduction with the maximum allowed aeration increase, giving the best margin to restore DO2 above 2.0 mg/L. The milder combined (x0.8, x1.15) risks leaving DO2 near or below the constraint if uptake is strongly feed-driven; stop is rejected outright since it produces zero counted production and discards in-progress product. The 4h lag on an extra assay (returning ~56h under KEEP) would leave the violation unaddressed for another cycle, so I act now rather than request the assay.
submission.uncertainty: The hidden relationship between feed rate, aeration, and OUR is unknown, so I cannot confirm that even x0.6 feed plus x1.15 air restores DO2 above 2.0 mg/L; if uptake is substrate-saturated, the feed cut may be insufficient and only stop would resolve the violation (at zero production). Product trajectory shows a lag/plateau (sources peaked ~8.3 g/L then declined to ~6.4-7.9 g/L by 96h), so even after re-oxygenation, final titer and total counted mass remain uncertain. Aeration headroom above 1.15x is also not established; if the air constraint binds, the expected DO recovery is overstated.

submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~46.2 h to 1.0-1.7 mg/L, well below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen operating minimum, and has stayed there for ~6 h — an active constraint violation that KEEP would perpetuate. Source batches never dropped below ~7 mg/L at comparable times, confirming a receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.40). Of the bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (feed ×0.6, air ×1.15) is the best trade-off: the forward model shows it yields the fewest below-limit hours (10.4 vs 13-17.4 for other actions), the smallest post-decision oxygen deficit (8.76 vs 11.4-13.3 mg·h/L), the highest minimum DO, and the highest retained product mass (~128.74 kg). Reduce_feed or increase_air alone address only one side of the oxygen balance; the strong combined action attacks both oxygen demand and supply. A stop is rejected because it zeroes counted production. Although the source-calibrated model is imperfect and predicts no action fully restores DO ≥ 2.0 mg/L, strong_feed_reduction dominates the relative ranking on every oxygen and mass metric.
submission.uncertainty: The physical forward model is calibrated on source batches with an estimated transfer multiplier of 0.40, so its absolute DO predictions likely underestimate the receiving vessel; its predicted absolute infeasibility under all actions should not be taken as truth. The relative ranking favoring strong_feed_reduction is more robust. There is residual uncertainty in hidden receiving parameters (OUR kinetics, Kla) — the strong feed cut may slow production rate somewhat, but model runs show no product-mass penalty vs alternatives, and mass is volume×concentration preserved. One extra assay was available but the online DO2 trace already gives decisive, timely evidence of the oxygen violation; a 4-h-turnaround assay would not change the intervention choice.

submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 abruptly fell at 46.2 h (12.9 → 8.2 mg/L) and has declined steadily to 7.4 mg/L by 52 h, while all three source batches at the same age still run ~10.5–11.5 mg/L. The product trajectory (P ≈ 3.03 g/L at 48 h, matching sources at ~3.0 g/L) shows production is on track, so the deviation is consistent with oxygen uptake demand outstripping transfer capacity in the receiving vessel, not a feed excess. increase_air raises the aeration factor within its bounded range (1.0 → 1.15), directly addressing the OTR shortfall without cutting feed and thus without sacrificing product mass, and keeps DO comfortably above the 2 mg/L minimum. Alternatives considered: KEEP risks continued DO decline and eventual oxygen-limited production; reduce_feed/combined/strong feed cuts reduce substrate and likely product mass without evidence of feed-related cause; stop yields zero counted production. Hidden receiving parameters may also include a different oxygen demand kinetics than sources, so the DO recovery magnitude is uncertain. Feed state is unobserved, so a covert feed excess cannot be fully excluded — if DO fails to recover post-intervention, feed reduction would be the next bounded step.

Combined intervention (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) attacks both sides of the oxygen balance with a bounded, reversible action: it restores DO2 margin above the floor while retaining 80% of feed and all accumulated product mass. Increase_air alone (15%) may be insufficient given the depth of the collapse; strong_feed_reduction sacrifices disproportionate production for margin we likely do not need; stop yields zero counted production. The receiving assay history is limited to 4 h lags, so product benefit is only indirectly estimated from the source trajectories.

submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation suffered an abrupt oxygen-transfer impairment at t≈50h (DO2 collapsed ~12→6 mg/L, while all source batches held ~10-11 mg/L at the same age). Product is also lagging the source envelope (2.65 vs ~3.0 g/L at 48h). The forward model indicates: keep leaves the batch oxygen-limited with marginal DO floor (2.09 nominal, down to 1.51 in sensitivity) and lowest product mass (~243 kg); increase_air alone is predicted infeasible (min DO 1.95 < 2.0 mg/L limit) because stimulating metabolism without reducing oxygen demand outstrips the degraded transfer; reduce_feed is feasible but leaves headroom unused; the combined action (feed ×0.8, air ×1.15) rebalances supply vs demand, stays feasible with a safer DO floor (~2.23) and yields the highest predicted product mass (~299 kg, +56 kg over keep). This preserves product mass, avoids an oxygen-constraint violation, and is a bounded, reviewable intervention.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is a source-calibrated nominal prediction, not the hidden receiving realization; its sensitivity members show DO floors down to ~1.48 mg/L for combined (4/5 feasible), so constraint risk is reduced but not eliminated. The root cause of the DO2 collapse (sensor artifact vs real transfer loss) is not fully resolved by available evidence; if it were a transient sensor fault, reduce_feed would sacrifice some product unnecessarily, but the anomaly has persisted ~2h across many samples, supporting a real impairment. Product-mass predictions span roughly 215-598 kg across sensitivity members.

proposal.rationale: The receiving batch underperforms all three source comparators: latest product assay 2.47 g/L at 48 h vs sources 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L (~18% lower), and its DO2 runs above source levels at matched times (lower oxygen uptake, slower metabolism). The nominal source-calibrated forward model predicts reduce_feed yields ~595.5 kg terminal product vs ~576.3 kg for KEEP (~+19 kg, ~3%), while remaining feasible with minimum DO ~10 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L limit. Combined offers no additional product mass over reduce_feed (identical 595.5 kg) and strong_feed_reduction/stop are unwarranted (stop = zero counted production; DO margin already large). The bounded reduce_feed intervention retains full product mass and avoids oxygen-constraint violations.
proposal.uncertainty: The forward model is a nominal source-calibrated prediction, not truth; hidden receiving parameters (transfer multiplier 1.144, change_h 44h) are estimated, and the ~19 kg gain is model-based. The observed 18% deficit is consistent with, but does not prove, a recoverable metabolic lag; if the lag is due to inoculum state rather than feed balance, gains may be smaller. DO margin is large across all sensitivity members, so oxygen-constraint risk from this action is low either way; the main downside risk is limited (mild feed reduction), making this a low-regret choice.

submission.rationale: Receiving fermentation shows a clear oxygen-supply deficit emerging at 48.2h: DO2 fell abruptly to ~7.75 mg/L and declined steadily to 6.94 mg/L by 52h, about 4 mg/L below comparable source batches at the same age (10.5-11 mg/L). This sustained downward trend indicates receiving oxygen demand exceeds current aeration, risking approach to the 2.0 mg/L minimum and slowing production (P(48h)=2.82 g/L already slightly below source trajectory). increase_air directly raises oxygen transfer with no loss of feed or product mass, unlike feed reductions, and is a bounded, reversible intervention.
submission.uncertainty: No direct OUR or kLa measurements; the abrupt DO2 step at 48.2h could partly be sensor-related, though the consistent 4h decline across many samples supports a real trend. Product assays lag 4h, so early impact on productivity can't be confirmed immediately. If aeration headroom is already saturated, increase_air may under-deliver and combined action would be the fallback.

evidence: Receiving DO2 step-down at t=48.2h: 12.10 -> 7.75 mg/L, continuing drift to 6.94 mg/L at t=52h
Source batches at t=48-52h show DO2 ~10.5-11.3 mg/L; no equivalent dip — receiving-specific transfer anomaly
Receiving P assay at t=48h (avail. 52h): 2.82 g/L, on track vs source 2.98-3.06 g/L
Forward model update: estimated oxygen transfer multiplier 0.632 with change at t=48h
Forward model predictions: combined = 598 kg, min DO 3.19, 5/5 sensitivity members feasible; keep = 284 kg, min DO 2.49, 4/5 feasible; increase_air min DO 2.38 (4/5); reduce_feed min DO 2.83 (4/5)
submission.rationale: At t=48 h the receiving DO2 stepped down from ~12.1 to ~7.7 mg/L and continues to fall (6.94 mg/L at t=52 h), while all three source batches at the same age hold ~10-11 mg/L — indicating a receiving-specific oxygen transfer impairment (forward model estimates transfer multiplier dropped to ~0.63). Product is on track (2.82 g/L at 48 h vs ~3.0 g/L source), so this is an oxygen-capacity fault, not a production failure. Source-calibrated forward model: keep gives 284 kg with post-decision min DO 2.49 mg/L and sensitivity members down to 1.8 (oxygen-constraint risk); increase_air (315 kg, min DO 2.38) and reduce_feed (340 kg, min DO 2.83) each leave sensitivity members near/below the 2.0 mg/L limit; combined (0.8 feed, 1.15 air) gives 598 kg product with min DO 3.19 mg/L and all 5 sensitivity members feasible. Combined therefore both restores oxygen margin and preserves/increases product mass, and avoids a stop (which would count zero production).
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal and source-calibrated, not the hidden realization; actual transfer impairment and kinetics may differ. If the DO2 dip were partly a sensor artifact, combined would still be safe (retains feed, only +15% air). If the transfer fault worsens beyond the modeled 0.63 multiplier, min DO2 could approach the 2.0 mg/L limit and a stronger action might be needed. Product mass gains from combined rely on model extrapolation; observed data alone only confirm the DO2 deficit and on-track product at 48 h.

evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 12.20 mg/L at 48.0 h falling to 5.25, 4.61, 4.28 and 4.27 mg/L at 48.2, 50.0, 51.6 and 52.0 h — a step collapse in oxygen transfer vs the 11–13 mg/L levels earlier in the run and vs the comparable source batches (~10–11 mg/L at 48–52 h).
Receiving delayed assay: P = 2.8925 g/L at t=48 h (available 52 h), consistent with source batches (2.98–3.06 g/L) — product formation on track, no feed-limitation problem pre-collapse.
Forward model KEEP: post-decision minimum DO 1.40 mg/L, below_limit 4.8 h, infeasible.
Forward model increase_air: minimum DO 1.45 mg/L, below_limit 5 h, infeasible.
Forward model combined: minimum DO 1.74 mg/L, below_limit 2.2 h, infeasible.
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: minimum DO 2.22 mg/L, below_limit 0 h, post_decision_feasible true, product mass 231.8 kg (highest of all actions).
Oxygen operating constraint: minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0 per task packet.
submission.rationale: At ~48.2 h the receiving vessel's DO2 dropped abruptly from ~12 mg/L to ~4–5 mg/L, indicating a step loss of oxygen-transfer capacity (transfer multiplier ~0.52) not seen in the source batches; DO2 continues to fall (4.27 mg/L at 52 h) toward the 2.0 mg/L operating limit. Product formation was on track (P=2.89 g/L at 48 h), so the failure is oxygen-transfer-limited growth, not feed insufficiency. The source-calibrated forward model predicts KEEP, increase_air, and combined all breach the 2.0 mg/L limit post-decision (min DO 1.40/1.45/1.74 mg/L respectively), while strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) is the only bounded action predicted to stay feasible (min DO 2.22 mg/L, zero below-limit hours, 4/5 sensitivity members feasible) while retaining full counted production and the highest predicted product mass (~232 kg vs ~183 kg for KEEP). A stop would zero counted production and was rejected. Rationale: cut oxygen demand enough to match the collapsed transfer capacity while modestly increasing aeration.

Strong feed reduction sacrifices some volumetric productivity (though predicted terminal mass is higher here because oxygen stress limits growth under KEEP), and the sensitivity members show minimum DO range 1.36–3.13 mg/L, so a small residual chance of constraint breach remains (1/5 members). submission.rationale: At decision time 52h, product is tracking the source batches (P=3.11 g/L at 48h), but the receiving vessel shows an abrupt DO2 step-down from ~11.8 to ~6.4 mg/L at t≈48.2h — a departure from all three source batches (10-11 mg/L at that age) and an inferred reduction in oxygen-transfer capacity (model-estimated multiplier 0.59). DO2 has stabilized at ~6.4-6.9 mg/L, above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, but the source-calibrated forward model projects continued decay toward the limit under KEEP (predicted minimum 2.34 mg/L, sensitivity members as low as 1.41 — violation risk). The combined action (feed ×0.8, aeration ×1.15) both restores DO headroom (predicted minimum 2.45 mg/L) and yields the highest predicted terminal product mass (~315 kg vs ~252 kg for KEEP), retaining full volume (no mass lost). Stop is rejected because it yields zero counted production. Reduce_feed alone or increase_air alone improves only one margin; combined is the bounded intervention that addresses both oxygen supply and demand while retaining product mass.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal and source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; its DO floor and mass predictions carry wide sensitivity ranges (e.g., KEEP min DO 1.41-2.43; combined 1.76-4.06), so benefit magnitudes are approximate. Observed DO2 has plateaued rather than continuing to fall, so the trajectory under KEEP might not decay as the model projects; however, even the model's own sensitivity members under KEEP dip near/below 2.0, so the combined action is a prudent risk-reduction with predicted upside rather than a mandatory correction. No further assay was requested because the latest P assay (48h, available 52h) already confirms production is on track and the 4h turnaround would not materially change the oxygen-margin decision.

Receiving delayed P assay: 3.113 g/L at t=48h (available 52h), consistent with source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L), so production is on track and stop would forfeit ~250+ kg of counted product
Forward model KEEP: product 251.8 kg, predicted post-decision minimum DO 2.34 mg/L (sensitivity range 1.41-2.43) — marginal vs the 2.0 mg/L operating minimum

Forward model reduce_feed: 280.9 kg at min DO 2.77; increase_air: 269.7 kg at min DO 2.16 — inferior mass/DO trade-off vs combined
arguments.rationale: At decision time 52h, product is tracking the source batches (P=3.11 g/L at 48h), but the receiving vessel shows an abrupt DO2 step-down from ~11.8 to ~6.4 mg/L at t≈48.2h — a departure from all three source batches (10-11 mg/L at that age) and an inferred reduction in oxygen-transfer capacity (model-estimated multiplier 0.59). DO2 has stabilized at ~6.4-6.9 mg/L, above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, but the source-calibrated forward model projects continued decay toward the limit under KEEP (predicted minimum 2.34 mg/L, sensitivity members as low as 1.41 — violation risk). The combined action (feed ×0.8, aeration ×1.15) both restores DO headroom (predicted minimum 2.45 mg/L) and yields the highest predicted terminal product mass (~315 kg vs ~252 kg for KEEP), retaining full volume (no mass lost). Stop is rejected because it yields zero counted production. Reduce_feed alone or increase_air alone improves only one margin; combined is the bounded intervention that addresses both oxygen supply and demand while retaining product mass.
arguments.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal and source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; its DO floor and mass predictions carry wide sensitivity ranges (e.g., KEEP min DO 1.41-2.43; combined 1.76-4.06), so benefit magnitudes are approximate. Observed DO2 has plateaued rather than continuing to fall, so the trajectory under KEEP might not decay as the model projects; however, even the model's own sensitivity members under KEEP dip near/below 2.0, so the combined action is a prudent risk-reduction with predicted upside rather than a mandatory correction. No further assay was requested because the latest P assay (48h, available 52h) already confirms production is on track and the 4h turnaround would not materially change the oxygen-margin decision.

evidence: Receiving DO2 steps from 11.76 mg/L (48.0 h) to 6.69 mg/L (48.2 h) and stays at 6.36 mg/L at 52.0 h, a sustained ~5 mg/L regime shift with no recovery

Receiving P assay trajectory (0 -> 0.0013 -> 1.09 -> 3.11 g/L) matches source batches, which peak near 8 g/L at 72-76 h during highest oxygen demand
DO2 minimum constraint is 2.0 mg/L; current margin is only ~4.4 mg/L entering the highest-demand production window
Allowed combined action is bounded: feed 0.8x, air 1.15x, retaining production and product mass unlike stop
submission.rationale: The receiving fermenter shows an abrupt, sustained ~5 mg/L DO2 drop at 48.2 h (11.8 to ~6.4 mg/L) that has not recovered over 4 hours, unlike all three source batches which held ~10.5-11.3 mg/L at the same age. Product is on a source-like trajectory (3.11 g/L at 48 h) and source history shows oxygen demand peaks in the 52-72 h window. DO2 is above the 2.0 mg/L minimum but margin is thin heading into the highest-demand phase. The combined intervention (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) is bounded and reversible: it reduces oxygen demand while increasing oxygen supply, protecting the constraint without stopping production (stop would yield zero counted production and discard accumulated product mass) and without the excessive throttling of strong_feed_reduction.
submission.uncertainty: The DO2 plateau at ~6.4 mg/L may be a stable new equilibrium rather than a deteriorating trend, in which case 'keep' would suffice; hidden receiving parameters (kLa, feed composition, organism state) are unobservable, so the 1.15x air ceiling may not fully restore margin if demand keeps rising; delayed assay clocks mean the true current product level is up to 4 h stale.

evidence: Receiving DO2 at t=52h = 9.63 mg/L vs sources 10.88/10.81/11.47 mg/L (persistent ~1.5 mg/L deficit entire run)
Receiving DO2 mid-run dip to ~6.96 mg/L at 27.6h vs sources' ~8.0-8.9 mg/L
Receiving P(48h)=2.87 g/L comparable to sources (2.98-3.06 g/L); source peak ~72h then decline
Forward model KEEP: 576.3 kg, min DO 6.09 mg/L; reduce_feed: 595.6 kg, min DO 7.01 mg/L, all sensitivity members feasible
Minimum DO limit 2.0 mg/L; no predicted violations in either case, but reduce_feed widens margin given the observed higher OUR in receiving
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 tracks ~1.2-1.8 mg/L below all three source batches throughout the run and dipped deeper (to ~7.0 mg/L) during the 24-28h demand event, indicating a higher effective metabolic/feed load in the receiving process. Product is on trajectory with sources (2.87 g/L at 48h) and sources peak near 72h, so preserving culture health through the production phase is key. A bounded 20% feed reduction (air unchanged) lowers oxygen demand and substrate burn-through risk while retaining product mass: the source-calibrated forward model predicts 595.6 kg vs 576.3 kg for KEEP, with a higher minimum DO (7.01 vs 6.09 mg/L) and all sensitivity members feasible. KEEP is feasible but leaves the thinnest oxygen margin and lowest predicted mass; stronger actions (strong_feed_reduction, stop) risk starving the culture or zero production and are unjustified since no oxygen-constraint violation is imminent.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not tuned to the hidden receiving realization; the true benefit magnitude of reduce_feed (predicted +19 kg, ~3%) is uncertain and could be smaller or slightly negative if the DO2 deficit reflects a transfer/scale difference rather than feed. However, both KEEP and reduce_feed are predicted feasible with wide margin over the 2.0 mg/L limit (worst sensitivity member ~5.0 mg/L for reduce_feed), so downside risk is low. No current oxygen violation exists; the main risk of inaction is faster substrate depletion and a lower terminal product mass.

submission.rationale: DO2 collapsed from ~9.5 to ~1.0 mg/L at 50.2 h and remains ~0.9 mg/L at the 52 h decision point — an acute oxygen-transfer limitation (model estimates transfer multiplier dropped to ~0.4) violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Product (3.11 g/L at 48 h) is still rising, so a stop would forfeit counted production. Among the bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (feed to 0.6×, air to 1.15×) most aggressively cuts oxygen uptake demand while raising supply: the nominal forward model shows it yields the highest minimum DO2 (~0.87 mg/L), the fewest post-decision below-limit hours (9.4 vs 13.2 for increase_air/combined), and retains essentially full product mass (~194 kg). No bounded action fully restores the 2.0 mg/L minimum, so this is damage limitation: recommend strong_feed_reduction plus urgent engineering investigation of the aeration/transfer fault.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; it flags all sensitivity members as infeasible even for strong_feed_reduction, so the true receiving-process response (hidden parameters, actual OUR and kLa after 50 h) is uncertain — actual recovery could be better or worse than the nominal 0.87 mg/L minimum. The cause of the transfer drop (equipment fault vs. rheology change) is unobserved; if the fault worsens, even feed cutback may not restore DO2, whereas if transient, the batch may recover faster than predicted. Assay data are delayed 4 h, so current biomass/product state at 52 h is inferred, not measured.

submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 shows a sharp, sustained step drop from ~11.6 to ~6.5 mg/L at 50.2 h that does not occur in any of the three source batches at the same process age (all ~10.8–11.5 mg/L), indicating a receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit. DO2 is still above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, and product (3.24 g/L at 48 h) is slightly ahead of source batches, so production is healthy and should not be throttled. A bounded 15% increase in air (1.0 feed, 1.15 air) directly addresses the deficit while retaining full feed and product mass; stronger feed cuts would sacrifice growth for an oxygen margin that is not yet threatened.
submission.uncertainty: The cause of the DO2 step-down is unknown (equipment fault, gas-transfer change, or metabolic demand shift); if it is a sensor artifact, extra air is harmless, but if DO2 continues falling despite +15% air, a feed reduction may be needed later. DO2 may also recover on its own, making the intervention merely margin-restoring rather than necessary. Only ~1.8 h of post-drop data is available.

arguments.rationale: Receiving DO2 shows a sharp, sustained step drop from ~11.6 to ~6.5 mg/L at 50.2 h that does not occur in any of the three source batches at the same process age (all ~10.8–11.5 mg/L), indicating a receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit. DO2 is still above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, and product (3.24 g/L at 48 h) is slightly ahead of source batches, so production is healthy and should not be throttled. A bounded 15% increase in air (1.0 feed, 1.15 air) directly addresses the deficit while retaining full feed and product mass; stronger feed cuts would sacrifice growth for an oxygen margin that is not yet threatened.
arguments.uncertainty: The cause of the DO2 step-down is unknown (equipment fault, gas-transfer change, or metabolic demand shift); if it is a sensor artifact, extra air is harmless, but if DO2 continues falling despite +15% air, a feed reduction may be needed later. DO2 may also recover on its own, making the intervention merely margin-restoring rather than necessary. Only ~1.8 h of post-drop data is available.

submission.rationale: The receiving fermenter showed an abrupt oxygen-demand step event at ~50.2 h (DO2 dropped ~11.6 → ~6.5 mg/L) that the air supply alone cannot cover as oxygen demand continues growing. The source-calibrated forward model predicts KEEP becomes oxygen-infeasible (minimum DO 1.90 mg/L < 2.0 limit, 0.4 h below-limit), while combined (feed ×0.8, air ×1.15) restores feasibility (minimum DO ~2.69 mg/L) and yields the highest product mass of the feasible bounded actions (≈330.7 kg vs 292.9 for reduce_feed and 278.5 for increase_air). Combined acts on both sides of the oxygen balance while retaining product mass; stop would count zero production and a stronger feed cut (0.6) risks sacrificing product unnecessarily. submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; its sensitivity members span minimum DO 1.70–4.36 mg/L under combined and product mass 234–597 kg, so feasibility is likely but not certain. Current DO2 has plateaued ~6.5 mg/L rather than continuing to fall, so part of the risk may be smaller than the model suggests; conversely if demand growth resumes (as the model estimates from the step change), KEEP would violate the floor. If an extra product assay were needed it would arrive in 4 h under KEEP, which carries oxygen-risk during the wait; I therefore act now on the current DO2 evidence.

This is a receiving-specific event — all three source batches show DO2 around 10–11 mg/L in the same window, so it is not a source-driven input pattern. The process is mid-production (receiving P = 3.04 g/L at 48 h, matching sources), so a stop would forfeit counted production and a strong feed cut (40%) would sacrifice biomass/product trajectory unnecessarily. A 15% air increase alone is uncertain to recover DO2 from ~1.3 to >2.0 given the unknown magnitude of the demand/transfer deficit; a feed reduction alone leaves the transfer deficit unaddressed. The combined intervention (20% feed reduction + 15% air increase) attacks both oxygen demand and supply with a bounded, moderate feed penalty, giving the best chance of restoring DO2 above 2.0 mg/L while retaining product mass. No extra assay was requested: the crisis signal is the online DO2 sensor, and the 4-hour assay turnaround would run the process under KEEP while already in violation.
submission.uncertainty: The hidden receiving kinetics are unknown, so it is uncertain whether +15% air with a 20% demand reduction is sufficient to lift DO2 from ~1.3 mg/L above 2.0 mg/L; if the underlying deficit is large (e.g., a much lower kLa in the receiving vessel), strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed) might have been necessary. Conversely, if the DO2 drop were a transient sensor artifact, a milder increase_air-only action would have sufficed and avoided any feed penalty. Feed reduction also carries a risk of reduced product formation over the remaining run, though the 20% cut is bounded and reversible in review.

protocol.primary_comparison: Same AI without supplied model versus same AI with source-calibrated imperfect model
protocol.claim_limit: Tests model access benefit to agents; does not test added agent value beyond conventional optimizer. Earlier optimizer comparison retained.
protocol.interpretation: Strata specify disturbance assumptions, not guaranteed recoverability; report realized finite-menu feasibility separately.
protocol.parameter_reference: Coefficients relative to fixed seed0 kinetics; private seed varies unobserved initial states independently. Ranges are synthetic assumptions informed by port variability, not validated physical transfer distributions.
protocol.measurement_policy: DO every0.2h with assumedSD0.15mg/L; P every12h,4h delay,assumedSD0.03g/L; one extra ideal P assay4h delay and20assumed work minutes. No perfect substrate or complete initial state.
protocol.limits: Simulated DO>=2mg/L; no measured product-quality conclusion. Stop counts zero product; earlier violations remain counted.
protocol.analysis: Report separate violation duration/deficit, mass, concentration, volume, unnecessary stops, decision/measurement time, tool/model calls, completion. No combined score. Average repetitions within scenario; paired scenario bootstrap20000 draws for descriptive contrasts. No sample extension.
protocol.failures: Retain every selected scenario including numerical-domain failures and failed submissions. No infrastructure retries in primary study. No failures relabeled as correct stops.
protocol.bounds_of_claim: Exploratory synthetic study; fixed initial/control family; model/evaluator share equations. Restricted research SDK, not end-to-end production OS validation.
